Includes all amendments approved up to and including amendments ratified by the General Assembly in 2026 I. THE KING AND HEAD OF THE CHURCH

Jesus Christ, upon whose shoulders the government rests, whose name is called Wonderful, Counselor, the Mighty God, the Everlasting Father, the Prince of Peace; of the increase of whose government and peace there shall be no end; who sits upon the throne of David, and upon His kingdom to order it and to establish it with judgment and justice from henceforth, even forever (Isaiah 9:6-7); having all power given unto Him in heaven and in earth by the Father, who raised Him from the dead and set Him at His own right hand, far above all principality and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come, and has put all things under His feet, and gave Him to be the Head over all things to the Church, which is His body, the fullness of Him that filleth all in all (Ephesians 1:20-23); He, being ascended up far above all heavens, that He might fill all things, received gifts for His Church, and gave all offices necessary for the edification of His Church and the perfecting of His saints (Ephesians 4:10-13).

Jesus, the Mediator, the sole Priest, Prophet, King, Saviour, and Head of the Church, contains in Himself, by way of eminency, all the offices in His Church, and has many of their names attributed to Him in the Scriptures. He is Apostle, Teacher, Pastor, Minister, Bishop and the only Lawgiver in Zion.

It belongs to His Majesty from His throne of glory to rule and teach the Church through His Word and Spirit by the ministry of men; thus mediately exercising His own authority and enforcing His own laws, unto the edification and establishment of His Kingdom.

Christ, as King, has given to His Church officers, oracles and ordinances; and especially has He ordained therein His system of doctrine, government, discipline and worship, all of which are either expressly set down in Scripture, or by good and necessary inference may be deduced therefrom; and to which things He commands that nothing be added, and that from them naught be taken away.

Since the ascension of Jesus Christ to heaven, He is present with the Church by His Word and Spirit, and the benefits of all His offices are effectually applied by the Holy Ghost.

relationships.title: Altering and Refining the Language of BCO 59

metadata.summary: The CCB found Calvary Presbytery's overture to revise BCO 59 in conflict with the Constitution, as proposed changes to marriage publication and consent conflicted with BCO Preliminary Principle 7, BCO 11-2, BCO 29-1, and WCF 20.2.

relationships.title: Teaching Approved Exceptions

metadata.summary: An overture requiring a presbytery to allow a candidate to teach all his exceptions before approving him was found in conflict, as it violated presbytery's right to set ordination qualifications.

relationships.title: Teaching Approved Exceptions

metadata.summary: A second overture on the same topic was found in conflict because it would compel a man to explain—or appear not to hold—a view his presbytery has already judged non-vital and approved.

relationships.title: Teaching Approved Exceptions

metadata.summary: An overture requiring teaching elders to explain all approved exceptions was found in conflict with BCO Preliminary Principle 1 and WCF 20, as it could compel a man to teach what he does not believe.

relationships.title: Subscription and Stating Exceptions to the Standards

metadata.summary: An overture from Grace Presbytery amending BCO Preface II, chapter 16, and BCO 21-4 regarding doctrinal subscription was found in conflict with the second ordination vow.

relationships.title: Procedure for Suspending Rules

metadata.summary: The CCB advised that delegates are bound to follow the Constitution as fully as possible and declined to affirm that rules must be suspended to obey Christ, directing any changes through proper amendment procedures.

relationships.title: BCO 40-5 Matter re Metropolitan NY

occurrences.excerpt: Because the RAO is not a part of the Constitution (BCO Preface III), the Constitutional provision that governs is BCO 40 (Review and Control, specifically BCO 40-5). That states in part:

metadata.synopsis: A BCO 40-5 citation arose from Metro New York Presbytery's failure to redress a session that allowed a woman to expound Scripture in place of the sermon preceding the Lord's Supper, held services without preaching, and celebrated the Supper without a preceding sermon. The SJC remitted the matter to the presbytery for constitutional resolution because the session's later no-exception response was clearly inadequate and the unapproved minutes were unclear. Presbytery must complete its work with TE Higgins and Trinity Presbyterian Church's session and report to the 51st General Assembly. A separate procedural note questioned the Assembly's direct referral but did not void it.

metadata.synopsis: A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination 'vetting' removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1's sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session's sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.

relationships.title: Larry Ball v. Westminster Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: A complaint challenged Westminster Presbytery's denial of a challenge to its May 15, 2001 plan to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC answered no: the Presbytery did not err, and denied the complaint. BCO 25's local-church withdrawal right and the BCO Preface's grassroots principles extend to presbyteries unless expressly excluded, so a presbytery may determine its own membership and affiliation. The plan did not 'act for' local churches; they retained rights to remain in the PCA or leave, and retained property and internal operations.

relationships.title: Marshall v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery

topics: suspension of session without due process
metadata.synopsis: Teaching Elder Wallace Marshall complained against the same Eastern Carolina Presbytery actions at Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church that were the subject of Case 90-4, filed separately as a Teaching Elder complainant. The SJC sustained this complaint on essentially the same grounds as Case 90-4, finding that the presbytery lacked authority to suspend the session without due process and to constitute itself as a 'Session Pro Tem.'
